summary.en: Ask whose examples are missing, who gave permission, and who can correct a harmful prediction.
summary.bn: কার উদাহরণ বাদ পড়েছে, অনুমতি আছে কি না আর ক্ষতিকর অনুমান কে শুধরাবে—এসব প্রশ্ন করো।

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: The robot chooses the same team
Look for the empty spaces in the records
Shortcuts that do not protect people

practice.title: Missing opportunity
practice.statementHtml: Explain why no late-bus race records cannot prove weak running ability.
hints: State what was observed and what was not.
practice.answerHtml: Only opportunities to record races are counted. No running times for late-bus children were observed. Give those children a suitable chance and review selection rather than treating absence as poor performance.

practice.title: A privacy alternative
practice.statementHtml: Replace a classroom face-collection game with an activity teaching the same pattern idea.
hints: Invent pictures rather than collect identities.
practice.answerHtml: Use drawings of pretend faces with varied hair, hats or shapes and fictional labels. The class can discuss pattern matching and errors without collecting classmates’ identifiable photos.

practice.title: Two error costs
practice.statementHtml: Compare hiding an ordinary message with missing an illness, and propose a safeguard for each.
practice.answerHtml: An ordinary message hidden as spam may cause missed information, so provide review and restoration. Missing illness can delay care, so require appropriate qualified assessment and a clear help route rather than relying on a classroom score.

practice.title: Real oversight
practice.statementHtml: Design an appeal route for a child excluded by a model-assisted team selection.
hints: A person must be able to act on the concern.
practice.answerHtml: Tell children who to contact, explain the observations used and invite correction of missing or wrong records. Give a responsible teacher time and authority to reconsider the decision and provide another fair opportunity. Merely approving the model’s answer is insufficient.

quiz.prompt: The race-record table gives three early-bus records and zero late-bus records. What can we conclude?
options: The recorded opportunities are unequal; late-bus running speed is unknown
Late-bus children definitely run slowly
The model has measured everyone fairly
Early arrival proves better athletic ability
quiz.explanation: Read what is counted: records of a chance to race. A missing measurement cannot establish how fast an unmeasured child runs.

caption.en: Recorded race opportunities, not running speeds: three early-bus records and no late-bus records.
caption.bn: এটি দৌড়ের সুযোগ, গতি নয়: আগের বাসে তিন রেকর্ড, দেরির বাসে নেই।

quiz.prompt: Why can copying old team selections preserve unfairness?
options: All old labels are automatically fair
Past selections may reflect unequal chances or favouritism
Computers remove the history inside labels
Correctly copying a decision proves the decision was justified
quiz.explanation: An accurate imitation can repeat an unfair process. Investigate the source and meaning of labels before using them for selection.

quiz.prompt: If the bus-arrival column is removed, does that supply missing race times?
options: Yes; missing children automatically gain recorded times
Yes; all related differences disappear
No; deleting a column cannot create absent observations
No; therefore nothing can ever improve the process
quiz.explanation: The lack of opportunity remains. Offer an appropriate measurement chance and review the process; other clues may also carry related patterns.

quiz.prompt: Which classroom activity collects less private information?
options: Uploading everyone’s real face without asking
Copying private messages into an unknown app
Publishing names and photos for a toy exercise
Sorting drawn pretend faces
quiz.explanation: Drawings can teach the intended idea without gathering identifiable faces. Choose less sensitive data when it answers the same question.

quiz.prompt: A classmate agrees to private classroom photo use. What about public uploading?
options: It is a different use that needs appropriate permission
The first agreement automatically covers it
The model’s predicted identity supplies consent
Removing a first name guarantees no one can recognise the face
quiz.explanation: Purpose, audience and sharing matter. A person can be recognisable even after a name is removed.

quiz.prompt: What makes consent informed rather than a vague yes?
options: Never being told who will receive the data
Understanding the stated purpose and how the information will be used
Being unable to decline an optional game
Assuming a friend’s permission covers everyone
quiz.explanation: A meaningful choice requires an understandable explanation. Children also need responsible adult protection under applicable rules.

quiz.prompt: Why should spam and medical prediction errors not be compared only by total correct guesses?
options: All mistakes have the same consequence
Medical scores never produce false alarms
The harms and people affected can differ greatly
An ordinary hidden message can never matter
quiz.explanation: Missing a notice may harm a deadline, while missing illness can delay care. False alarms can also hurt, so safeguards must fit the context.

quiz.prompt: What should a child do with a medical model score?
options: Declare a classmate ill from the score
Ignore all symptoms because a model might err
Share someone’s health record to ask the class
Leave diagnosis to qualified assessment rather than treating the score as a diagnosis
quiz.explanation: The lesson compares error costs; it does not turn a classroom model into clinical evidence. Appropriate professionals remain responsible for assessment.

quiz.prompt: A teacher says “the model chose, so nobody can change it”. What is missing?
options: A reachable human review with authority to correct the decision
A promise to make the model name longer
Permission to delete every complaint
A reason to stop explaining selections
quiz.explanation: People choose and operate the system. Oversight needs information, time and the power to change an unfair or mistaken decision.

quiz.prompt: Do equal selection totals by themselves prove that the entire process is fair?
options: Yes; one matching count settles all fairness questions
No; context, opportunity and effects still need investigation
Yes; no one needs a chance to appeal
No; counts can never reveal useful warning signs
quiz.explanation: Counts can flag issues but cannot tell the whole story. Investigate how examples were collected and what the decision does to people.

keyPoints.en: Missing examples can hide missing opportunities.
keyPoints.bn: তথ্যের ঘাটতির পেছনে সুযোগের ঘাটতি থাকতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Old answers can preserve unfair treatment.
keyPoints.bn: পুরোনো উত্তরে অন্যায় থেকে যেতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Personal data needs a clear purpose and appropriate permission.
keyPoints.bn: ব্যক্তিগত তথ্যে উদ্দেশ্য আর উপযুক্ত অনুমতি লাগে।
কম সংগ্রহ privacy রক্ষা করতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Mistakes have different costs for different people.
keyPoints.bn: একেক ভুলে একেক মানুষের আলাদা ক্ষতি হয়।

keyPoints.en: Human review needs real authority to correct a decision.
Honest limits and appeal routes make tools easier to question.
keyPoints.bn: সৎ সীমা আর আপত্তির পথ সিস্টেমকে প্রশ্ন করতে সাহায্য করে।

examQuestions.question: Explain bias, privacy and consent using the school-game story.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Bias can arise when recorded examples systematically miss late-bus children or copy unfair past choices. Privacy concerns control of personal records such as identifiable photos. Consent is informed permission for a stated use and does not silently extend to public sharing.

examQuestions.question: Three early-bus children have race records and three late-bus children have none. Count recorded and unrecorded children, then state what cannot be inferred.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Three children are recorded and three unrecorded. The unrecorded children’s speeds are unknown. Counting missing opportunities does not measure poor ability or prove any particular future team should be selected.

examQuestions.question: Write five questions for an imaginary smart school app.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Ask what it predicts, whose examples supplied its evidence, what permission covers the records, who may be harmed by an error and how a person can challenge or correct the result. Each question targets a concrete responsibility rather than accepting a claim of perfect intelligence.

examQuestions.question: Why is “the model said so” an inadequate explanation for a harmful decision?
examQuestions.answerHtml: People select the task, data and way predictions are used. They remain responsible for explanation, safeguards and correction. Affected people need a reachable review process whose reviewer has information and power to change the outcome.
